question: I have only Basic Autoplan and caused a crash in B.C. What coverage distinction matters before I assume my own car's repairs will be paid?
generated_answer:
The difference between Basic Autoplan and regular coverage lies in the types of damages or incidents covered. Basic Autoplan typically includes basic third-party liability, which covers damages to others, but may not cover damages to your own vehicle. If you caused the accident and have only Basic Autoplan, you may be responsible for repairing your own car.

However, if you were not at fault, the other party's insurance may cover your repairs. It's essential to review your policy details and contact your insurance provider to understand what is covered and what is not. They will guide you on how to proceed with your claim.

If you are found at fault, you may need to pay out of pocket for your vehicle's repairs unless you have additional coverage, such as collision or comprehensive coverage, which may be included in a regular Autoplan policy.

It's crucial to carefully review your policy and communicate with your insurance provider to determine the next steps for your specific situation. They will help you navigate the claims process and determine if any coverage distinctions apply to your case.
